newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF CHELSEA PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF CHELSEA PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Chelsea players ahead of Sunday's F.A. Cup semifinal against Wimbledon at Highbury:

Frode Grodas, goalkeeper, age 27. Norwegian who joined from Lillestroem. In competition with Kevin Hitchcock for the first-choice keeper's spot. Came on as a substitute for Hitchcock in a match in late February and has kept his place ever since.

Kevin Hitchcock, goalkeeper, age 34. Stepped into the Chelsea first team for an F.A. Cup tie against Newcastle last season and saved two penalties in a dramatic shoot-out. Out of favour and suffering from a shoulder injury. Eight seasons of experience at the Bridge.

Scott Minto defender/midfielder, 25. Natural wing-back whose career at Chelsea has been blighted by injury since his arrival from first division Charlton. Nevertheless, has struck up a fluid partnership with Italy's Roberto di Matteo on the left flank. Scored a rare goal against Wimbledon earlier this season.

Steve Clark, defender, 33. Scottish international whose days in the first team looked numbered when Chelsea signed right-back Dan Petrescu. Proved his adaptabilty by moving across to the left where he has enjoyed one of the finest of his 10 seasons at Stamford Bridge.

Franck Leboeuf, defender, 29. Centre-back who joined from Strasbourg last summer. The organiser in the Chelsea back line and dangerous coming forward too. But will not play on Sunday after limping out of the F.A. Cup sixth round defeat of Portsmouth.
Frank Sinclair, defender, 25. Burly full-back who has learned a lot from playing alongside Leboeuf and Clarke this year.

Dan Petrescu, defender/midfielder, 29. Classy right-sided wing-back signed by Glenn Hoddle last season. Gets forward at every opportunity and uses space intelligently. An automatic choice for Romania, for whom he has been capped over 50 times.
Erland Johnsen, defender/midfielder, 30. Joined from Bayern Munich. Often used as a substitute but could start on Sunday owing to Leboeuf's absence.

Roberto di Matteo, midfielder, 26. Signed from Lazio after a successful European championship for Italy last June. Has scored a number of superb goals from the edge of the box since then. Born in Switzerland, turned down an offer to play for the Swiss national side. Has said his dream is to have five children.

Eddie Newton, midfielder, 25. Hard tackler who plays the holding role in Chelsea's midfield allowing di Matteo and Dennis Wise to sweep forward. Broke his right shin last season and has been out since early March this year due to a knee operation. Likely to be back in the starting line-up on Sunday though.

Dennis Wise, midfielder, 30. Played 135 league games for Wimbledon before joining Chelsea. Dynamic club captain always in the thick of things. Born within a couple of miles of the Bridge. Makes up for his lack of height (167 cm) by packing a great right-foot strike. On the fringes of the England squad last season.
Craig Burley, midfielder, 25. Hard-working Scottish international. Will want to forget his role in the F.A. Cup semifinal of last season. His miscued backpass set up Manchester United's winner.

Mark Hughes, forward, 33. Scored in both Chelsea's previous F.A. Cup ties against Wimbledon. Since joining Chelsea in the summer of 1995 "Sparky" has continually delivered the goods despite competition from Italians Gianluca Vialli and Gianfranco Zola. Currently keeping Vialli on the bench. Muscular and stubborn on the pitch, quietly spoken and articulate off it. Played at Barcelona from 1986-88. Capped over 60 times for Wales.

Gianfranco Zola, forward, 30. Diminutive Sardinian who has been spellbinding since his transfer from Parma late last year, ousting compatriot Gianluca Vialli up front. Lethal from free-kicks. His goal for Italy floored England at Wembley a week ago.

Gianluca Vialli, forward, 32. Joined within days of captaining Juventus to the European Cup last year. Lured to London on a free transfer by his old friend Gullit. Outspoken and principled, he has expressed his displeasure at spending so much time on the bench this season. Despite his obvious talent has become something of an unlucky mascot for Chelsea who have an uncanny knack of losing when he plays.

Ruud Gullit, midfielder/manager, 34. has transformed Chelsea since arrival from Italy, bringing half of serie A to west London in his wake. Still a wonderful talent on the increasingly rare occasions he plays but will miss the rest of the season with a fractured ankle and will have to watch the semifinal from the bench. Scored against Wimbledon in the sixth round last season and also in the semifinal against Manchester United. Enjoying a blossoming career as an articulate television soccer pundit.
